title: 15. System Design Case Studies: Design Pastebin
summary: Design a Pastebin-style service (à la pastebin.com, GitHub Gist, hastebin) where a user pastes a blob of text, receives a unique short URL, and anyone with the link can view the paste with optional syntax highlighting,…
objectives: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)

sections.title: Step 1: Clarify Requirements (5 min)
sections.body:
> **In one line:** Design a Pastebin-style service (à la pastebin.com, GitHub Gist, hastebin) where a user pastes a blob of text, receives a unique short URL, and anyone with the link can view the paste with optional syntax highlighting, expiration, and password protection. ---

### Functional Requirements
- User pastes plain text or code (≤ 2 MB per paste for free tier, ≤ 50 MB for pro).
- System returns a unique URL like `https://paste.example/abc123`.
- Anyone with the link can view the paste in raw or rendered (syntax-highlighted) form.
- Optional expiration: 10 min, 1 h, 1 day, 1 week, never (default = 1 month).
- Optional password protection (paste is encrypted server-side, prompt for password on view).
- Optional syntax highlighting (200+ languages via Pygments / highlight.js).
- Optional "private" pastes visible only to the owner.
- Pro users can edit and version their pastes (Gist-style).
- Raw endpoint `GET /raw/{id}` returns the plaintext body for curling / scripting.
- Web UI shows a "recent public pastes" feed (capped to last 100, time-decayed).

### Non-Functional Requirements
- **Availability** 99.9% (≈ 8 h 45 m downtime/year). Reads must survive writes being degraded.
- **Latency** p99 < 100 ms for paste view (rendered HTML cached), < 50 ms for raw.
- **Read:write ratio ≈ 50:1** (classic read-heavy) — most pastes are viewed many times.
- **Write throughput** ~5 M pastes/day ≈ 60 writes/s avg, ~600/s peak.
- **Read throughput** ~250 M views/day ≈ 3 000 QPS avg, ~15 000 QPS peak.
- **Storage**: average paste size 10 KB (most are small code snippets) ⇒ 5 M × 10 KB = 50 GB/day ⇒ 91 TB over 5 years. Pro pastes (50 MB) are rare but skew the distribution — store them on S3, not in the metadata DB.
- **Durability** 11 nines for paste content (loss = lost code = angry developers).
- **Security**: SQL/HTML injection prevention, content scanning for malware/PII, rate-limit anonymous writes, optional TLS-only.
- **Observability**: per-paste view counter, content-type distribution, hot-paste alerts.

### Back-of-Envelope Estimation
- 5 M new pastes/day × 30 days = 150 M active pastes/month.
- 250 M views/day ÷ 5 M new = average 50 views/paste, but distribution is power-law (top 1% pastes get 80% of views).
- Storage growth: 50 GB/day → 18 TB/year on hot tier; archive pastes untouched for 90 days to S3 IA, untouched for 1 year to S3 Glacier.
- Bandwidth: 250 M views × 10 KB = 2.5 TB/day egress; CDN absorbs 70% → 750 GB/day origin egress.
- Metadata DB size: 5 M × 500 B = 2.5 GB/day ⇒ 4.5 TB over 5 years — fits on a sharded Postgres or DynamoDB.

### Scope
- **In scope**: paste create/view/expire, syntax highlighting, password protection, raw endpoint, basic versioning for pro, scaling, CDN caching, archival to cold storage.
- **Out of scope**: real-time collaborative editing, full Git integration, in-browser code execution (à la CodeSandbox), full-text search across all pastes (covered briefly but not deeply built).

sections.title: Step 2: High-Level Architecture (10 min)
sections.body:
### Components 1. **Global DNS + Anycast** (Route 53) — routes to nearest POP. 2. **CDN** (CloudFront / Cloudflare) — caches rendered HTML of public pastes for 10 min; raw endpoint cached for 60 s. 3. **API Gateway** (Kong / Envoy) — TLS, rate limit (anonymous 10 pastes/hour), WAF, JWT auth for pro users. 4. **Web app tier** — stateless Go services: `paste-create-svc` and `paste-view-svc` autoscaled independently. 5. **Paste metadata DB** — DynamoDB / Cassandra for `paste_id → metadata + small content` (< 4 KB), or sharded PostgreSQL if relational queries (owner, tags) are needed. 6. **Object storage** (S3) — paste bodies ≥ 4 KB stored as `s3://pastes/{prefix}/{id}.txt`. Lifecycle policy moves to S3 IA after 90 days, Glacier after 1 year. 7. **Redis cluster** — caches rendered HTML, raw text, view counters (INCR), rate-limit tokens. 8. **Highlight worker pool** — Pygments / highlight.js running server-side; produces cached HTML. Triggered async via Kafka on first view. 9. **Kafka** — `paste-events` topic (create, view, expire) feeding analytics, search indexing, malware scan. 10. **Search index** (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch) — indexes public paste text for `/search?q=...` (pro feature). 11. **PostgreSQL** — user accounts, pro subscriptions, paste ownership, billing. 12. **Malware scanner** — ClamAV or AWS GuardDuty Malware Protection; scans paste bodies before they're listed in public feed. ### Mermaid Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR U([User / Browser / curl]) --> DNS[Route 53] DNS --> CDN[CloudFront / Cloudflare CDN] CDN -->|"cache hit: rendered HTML"| U CDN -->|cache miss| GW[API Gateway + WAF] GW --> CREATE[paste-create-svc] GW --> VIEW[paste-view-svc] CREATE --> IDS[Snowflake ID gen] CREATE --> PG[(PostgreSQL
accounts/owners)] CREATE --> S3[(S3
paste bodies)] CREATE --> DDB[(DynamoDB
paste metadata)] CREATE --> K[(Kafka
paste-events)] VIEW --> REDIS[(Redis cluster
rendered/raw cache)] REDIS --> DDB REDIS --> S3 VIEW --> K K --> HW[Highlight worker
Pygments] HW --> REDIS K --> SCAN[Malware scan] K --> ES[(OpenSearch
full-text index)] K --> AGG[Flink aggregator
view counts] AGG --> CH[(ClickHouse
analytics)] DDB --> ARCH[Archival job
-> S3 IA/Glacier] ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` +---------------+ | Route 53 | Anycast DNS +-------+-------+ | +-------v-------+ | CDN edge | cache rendered HTML +---+-------+---+ hit | | miss | +----+ +---v-----------+ | | API Gateway | | 301 | (Kong + WAF) | | +--+---------+--+ v | | +-------+--+ +----v---+ +---v--------+ | browser | | POST | | GET /{id} | +----------+ |/pastes | | paste-view | +---+----+ +---+--------+ | | +--------+--+ +--v------+ |Snowflake ID| | Redis | +--------+--+ | cluster | | +--+------+ +--------v--+ | | DynamoDB |<------+ | metadata | +-----+-----+ | +-----v-----+ | S3 bodies | -> 90d -> S3 IA -> 1y -> Glacier +-----------+ | +-----v-----+ | Kafka | +-----+-----+ | +-------+-------+-------+-------+ | | | | | +----v---+ +v----+ +v----+ +v-----+ +v----+ |Highligh| |Scan | |OpenS| |Flink | |Click| |Worker | |AV | |earch| |Agg | |House| +--------+ +-----+ +-----+ +------+ +-----+ ``` ### Request Flow Walkthrough 1. **Create**: Client `POST /pastes {content, language, ttl, password?}` → API Gateway rate-limits → `paste-create-svc` allocates a Snowflake ID, base62-encodes → `abc123`. If body ≥ 4 KB → write to `s3://pastes/ab/abc123.txt`; else inline in DynamoDB. Metadata row written conditionally. Event published to Kafka `paste-events`. Returns `https://paste.example/abc123`. 2. **View**: `GET /abc123` → CDN edge. If cached rendered HTML → return 200 in < 5 ms. On miss → `paste-view-svc` → Redis (raw + rendered cache) → DynamoDB metadata → S3 body (if not inline) → if first view, async-trigger highlight worker via Kafka → return HTML with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=600`. 3. **Highlight worker**: Consumes `paste-created` and `paste-first-view` events, runs Pygments to produce HTML, stores back to Redis (5 min TTL) and a long-term S3 object `s3://rendered/ab/abc123.html`. 4. **Expiration**: DynamoDB TTL attribute `ttl_epoch`. Reaper deletes expired rows within 48 h; on delete, a stream triggers cache invalidation and S3 body deletion. 5. **Analytics**: Every view publishes a `paste-viewed` event to Kafka; Flink computes per-paste view counts and writes to ClickHouse hourly.

sections.title: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
sections.body:
### Tables / Schema

**DynamoDB — `pastes` (metadata + small bodies)**
```
PK: paste_id (S)               // "abc123"
attributes:
  owner_id        (S)          // "anon" or account id
  language        (S)          // "python", "text", "go"
  visibility      (S)          // "public" | "unlisted" | "private"
  password_hash   (S)          // bcrypt hash, absent if unprotected
  content_inline  (S)          // if body < 4 KB; else S3 key
  s3_key          (S)          // "ab/abc123.txt"
  size_bytes      (N)
  created_at      (N)
  expires_at      (N)
  ttl_epoch       (N)          // DynamoDB TTL attribute
  view_count      (N)          // updated async by Flink
  version         (N)          // bumped on edit (pro)
```

**DynamoDB GSI — `pastes_by_owner`** (for "my pastes" page)
```
PK: owner_id (S)
SK: created_at (N)
projected: paste_id, language, size_bytes
```

**DynamoDB GSI — `recent_public`** (for the homepage feed)
```
PK: "PUBLIC" (constant, single partition — capped)
SK: created_at (N)
projected: paste_id, language, size_bytes
```

**PostgreSQL — `accounts` / `subscriptions`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE accounts (
    id           BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    email        TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    plan         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free',  -- free | pro
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
    account_id   BIGINT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES accounts(id),
    stripe_id    TEXT,
    renewal_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    max_paste_kb INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 51200      -- 50 MB for pro
);
```

**S3 layout — paste bodies**
```
s3://pastes-bucket/
   ab/abc123.txt                 # raw body
   ab/abc123.html                # rendered HTML (long-term cache)
   ab/abc123_v2.txt              # pro versioning
```

**OpenSearch — `pastes` index** (public pastes only)
```json
{
  "paste_id": "abc123",
  "language": "python",
  "content": "def hello():...",    // analyzed text
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T...",
  "owner_id": "u42"
}
```

### Indexes
- DynamoDB PK `paste_id` ⇒ O(1) lookup by ID.
- GSI `pastes_by_owner` enables the "my pastes" page without scanning.
- GSI `recent_public` is a single hot partition — capped at 100 items (TTL prunes old entries) so it's bounded.
- OpenSearch inverted index supports full-text search across millions of public pastes.
- S3 lifecycle: `Standard → IA (90 d) → Glacier (1 y) → Delete (3 y)`.

### Storage Choice
- **DynamoDB** for metadata: massive write scale, single-key access, TTL for expiration, no schema migrations.
- **S3** for bodies: 11-nines durability, virtually unlimited, lifecycle policies for cost tiering. S3 byte-range fetch supports partial reads of large pastes.
- **Redis** for hot rendered HTML and raw text — sub-ms reads, 70% hit rate.
- **PostgreSQL** for accounts/billing — relational integrity, ACID for money.
- **OpenSearch** for search — inverted index purpose-built for full-text.

sections.title: Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)
sections.body:
### API Design
```
POST /api/v1/pastes
  body: { "content": "...", "language": "python", "ttl_seconds": 86400,
          "visibility": "unlisted", "password": "secret?", "title": "..." }
  resp: { "id": "abc123", "url": "https://paste.example/abc123",
          "raw_url": "https://paste.example/raw/abc123", "expires_at": "..." }

GET /{id}                      # rendered HTML page (200) or 404 / 410 Gone (expired)
GET /raw/{id}                  # plaintext body, content-type: text/plain
GET /api/v1/pastes/{id}        # JSON metadata (owner only if private)

POST /api/v1/pastes/{id}/verify
  body: { "password": "secret" }  resp: 200 + content, or 401

PATCH /api/v1/pastes/{id}      # pro: edit content -> bumps version
DELETE /api/v1/pastes/{id}     # owner only

GET /api/v1/users/me/pastes?cursor=...   # paginated "my pastes"
GET /api/v1/search?q=...&lang=python     # full-text search (pro)
```

### Key Algorithms

**1. ID generation — Snowflake + base62.** Same approach as URL shortener. 8-char base62 = 218 T codes. Paste IDs are also used as S3 keys.

**2. Body routing (inline vs S3).** If `size < 4 KB` → store inline in DynamoDB (saves a round-trip on read, costs ~same as S3). Else → S3. Threshold tunable based on observed latency vs cost.

**3. Syntax highlighting.** Lazy: on first view, publish `highlight-requested` event to Kafka. Highlight worker runs Pygments (Python) with a 5 s timeout — large pastes time out and fall back to plain `<pre>`. Rendered HTML cached in Redis (5 min TTL) and S3 (long-term, key `{id}.html`). Subsequent views serve from Redis or S3 directly.

**4. Password protection.** Generate a random 256-bit key per paste, encrypt body with AES-256-GCM. The key is derived from the user's password via PBKDF2 (100 k iterations). Store only the ciphertext + salt + nonce — server cannot decrypt without the password. On view, client posts password, server derives key, decrypts, returns plaintext. Trade-off: server-side password check vs client-side decryption — we pick server-side for simplicity.

**5. Expiration.** DynamoDB TTL attribute = `expires_at` in epoch seconds. TTL reaper deletes within 48 h; for instant expiration we also check `expires_at < now()` on read and return 410 Gone. On TTL deletion, DynamoDB Streams emit an event → S3 body deletion + cache invalidation.

**6. View counter.** Async: every view publishes `paste-viewed` event to Kafka; Flink consumes, increments `view_count` in DynamoDB every 5 s (batched to avoid hot-key writes). Redis also holds a fast approximate counter for the homepage.

**7. Archival.** Nightly job: for pastes untouched in 90 days, move S3 object from Standard → IA (saves 40% cost). After 1 year → Glacier Deep Archive (saves 95%). DynamoDB row stays (small) so the link still resolves; lazy restore on access.

```python
# pastebin.py — core: paste creation, inline-vs-S3 routing, password encryption
import os, json, time, base64, hashlib, threading
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf.pbkdf2 import PBKDF2HMAC
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes

EPOCH = 1_700_000_000_000
MACHINE_ID = 7
MAX_SEQ = (1 << 12) - 1
B62 = "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
INLINE_THRESHOLD = 4 * 1024     # 4 KB
PBKDF2_ITERS = 100_000

class Snowflake:
    def __init__(self, mid):
        self.mid, self.seq, self.last, self.lock = mid, 0, -1, threading.Lock()
    def next_id(self) -> int:
        with self.lock:
            ts = int(time.time()*1000) - EPOCH
            if ts == self.last:
                self.seq = (self.seq + 1) & MAX_SEQ
                if self.seq == 0:
                    while ts <= self.last: ts = int(time.time()*1000) - EPOCH
            else: self.seq = 0
            self.last = ts
            return (ts << 22) | (self.mid << 10) | self.seq

def to_base62(n, length=8):
    s = ""
    while n: s = B62[n%62] + s; n //= 62
    return s.rjust(length, "0")[-length:]

def derive_key(password: str, salt: bytes) -> bytes:
    kdf = PBKDF2HMAC(algorithm=hashes.SHA256(), length=32, salt=salt, iterations=PBKDF2_ITERS)
    return kdf.derive(password.encode())

def encrypt(content: bytes, password: str):
    salt = os.urandom(16); nonce = os.urandom(12)
    key = derive_key(password, salt)
    ct = AESGCM(key).encrypt(nonce, content, None)
    return salt, nonce, ct

def decrypt(salt, nonce, ct, password: str) -> bytes:
    key = derive_key(password, salt)
    return AESGCM(key).decrypt(nonce, ct, None)

class S3Mock:
    def __init__(self): self.store = {}
    def put(self, key, body): self.store[key] = body
    def get(self, key): return self.store.get(key)

class DynamoMock:
    def __init__(self): self.items = {}
    def put(self, item):
        if item["paste_id"] in self.items: return False
        self.items[item["paste_id"]] = item; return True
    def get(self, pid): return self.items.get(pid)
    def delete(self, pid): self.items.pop(pid, None)

class PasteService:
    def __init__(self, s3, ddb, snow):
        self.s3, self.ddb, self.snow = s3, ddb, snow

    def create(self, content: str, language="text", ttl_seconds=2592000,
               visibility="unlisted", password=None, owner="anon"):
        body = content.encode("utf-8")
        paste_id = to_base62(self.snow.next_id())
        s3_key = f"{paste_id[:2]}/{paste_id}.txt"
        # routing decision
        if len(body) <= INLINE_THRESHOLD and password is None:
            content_field, s3_field = body.decode("utf-8", "replace"), None
        else:
            self.s3.put(s3_key, body)
            content_field, s3_field = None, s3_key
        # password encryption (only meaningful for S3 path; we re-route)
        pw_hash, salt, nonce, ct = None, None, None, None
        if password:
            salt, nonce, ct = encrypt(body, password)
            self.s3.put(s3_key, ct)             # overwrite with ciphertext
            content_field, s3_field = None, s3_key
            pw_hash = hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]
        now = int(time.time()*1000)
        item = {
            "paste_id": paste_id, "owner_id": owner, "language": language,
            "visibility": visibility, "password_hash": pw_hash,
            "content_inline": content_field, "s3_key": s3_field,
            "size_bytes": len(body), "created_at": now,
            "expires_at": now + ttl_seconds*1000,
            "salt": salt, "nonce": nonce,
            "view_count": 0, "version": 1,
        }
        assert self.ddb.put(item), "collision"
        return {"id": paste_id, "url": f"https://paste.example/{paste_id}",
                "expires_at": item["expires_at"]}

    def view(self, paste_id, password=None):
        item = self.ddb.get(paste_id)
        if not item: return None, "not_found"
        if item["expires_at"] < int(time.time()*1000):
            self.ddb.delete(paste_id); return None, "gone"
        if item["password_hash"]:
            if not password: return None, "auth_required"
            if hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest()[:32] != item["password_hash"]:
                return None, "auth_failed"
        if item["content_inline"]:
            return item["content_inline"], None
        ct = self.s3.get(item["s3_key"])
        if item["password_hash"]:
            return decrypt(item["salt"], item["nonce"], ct, password).decode(), None
        return ct.decode(), None

if __name__ == "__main__":
    svc = PasteService(S3Mock(), DynamoMock(), Snowflake(MACHINE_ID))
    r1 = svc.create("print('hello')", language="python", ttl_seconds=60)
    print("created:", r1)
    print("view:", svc.view(r1["id"]))
    r2 = svc.create("x"*5000, password="secret", ttl_seconds=60)
    print("protected:", r2["id"])
    print("no pw:", svc.view(r2["id"]))
    print("wrong pw:", svc.view(r2["id"], password="nope"))
    print("right pw:", svc.view(r2["id"], password="secret"))
    r3 = svc.create("tiny", ttl_seconds=-1)   # already expired
    print("expired:", svc.view(r3["id"]))
```

Sample output:
```
created: {'id': 'nYunnITg', 'url': 'https://paste.example/nYunnITg', 'expires_at': 1786715476470}
view: ("print('hello')", None)
protected: nYunnITh
no pw: (None, 'auth_required')
wrong pw: (None, 'auth_failed')
right pw: ('xxxxx...', None)
expired: (None, 'gone')
```

sections.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min)
sections.body:
### Scaling Challenges
- **Read-heavy load (50:1)**: CDN edge + Redis absorb 90%+ of reads. DynamoDB on-demand scales per-partition; we provision ~3 000 RCUs baseline.
- **Hot pastes**: a viral paste can spike from 10 QPS to 100 k QPS. CDN caches rendered HTML for 10 min — most requests never reach origin. For raw endpoint, set `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, s-maxage=300`.
- **Large paste storage**: a single 50 MB pro paste is rare but can blow up DynamoDB item size (400 KB limit) — that's why we route to S3 at 4 KB threshold. S3 byte-range fetches let us stream large pastes.
- **Highlight worker back-pressure**: 5 M pastes/day but only ~10% are viewed enough to warrant pre-rendering. Workers consume from Kafka with 4 parallelism per pod; autoscale by consumer lag.
- **Search index lag**: OpenSearch indexing is eventually consistent — a freshly-created public paste may take 5 s to be searchable. Acceptable for our SLO.
- **Archival cost**: 91 TB over 5 years on S3 Standard = $2 700/month. Lifecycle to Glacier cuts it to $270/month. Worth the 12-hour restore latency for old pastes.

### Caching Strategy
- **Multi-tier cache**: CDN edge (10 min, public pastes only) → Redis cluster (5 min, raw + rendered) → DynamoDB → S3 (cold).
- **Cache-aside**: writes do NOT populate cache. First read populates asynchronously — highlight worker produces HTML in parallel.
- **Negative cache**: 404 for unknown IDs cached 10 s (prevents enumeration/probing).
- **Stale-while-revalidate**: CDN serves stale HTML for up to 1 min after TTL while refreshing in background — smooths spike latency.

### Failure Modes
| Failure | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Redis cluster down | p99 latency jumps from 5 ms to 50 ms | 3-node Redis Cluster + failover; DynamoDB direct read still works |
| S3 outage (rare) | Large paste bodies unreadable | Inline threshold raised to 64 KB as fallback; serve "paste temporarily unavailable" |
| DynamoDB region outage | Cannot create new pastes | Multi-region Global Tables; reads from replica region |
| Kafka broker down | Highlight rendering + analytics lag, view path unaffected | 3 brokers RF=3, min ISR=2; consumers resume from last committed offset |
| Highlight worker OOM | Big paste crashes worker | 5 s timeout + 5 MB body cap for highlighting; plain `<pre>` fallback |
| Malware in paste | Public feed shows malicious content | Sync ClamAV scan before listing in feed; async scan within 60 s of creation |
| TTL reaper lag | Expired pastes visible past `expires_at` | Read-time check `expires_at < now()` returns 410 immediately |

quiz.question: Why is Pastebin read-heavy, and how does that shape the architecture?
options: PostgreSQL FTS works fine up to ~10 M rows but starts to degrade at 100 M+ — index rebuilds are slow, ranking quality is poor, and sharding requires Citus or manual…
S3 lifecycle policies automate tiered storage. A new paste body lands in S3 Standard ($0.023/GB/month).
Two reasons. (1) Latency: an inline read is a single DynamoDB GetItem (~5 ms), vs DynamoDB + S3 GetObject (~25 ms).
The 50:1 read:write ratio comes from human behavior: a developer writes a paste once and shares the link with a team, a forum, or social media — dozens to thousands of…
quiz.explanation: The 50:1 read:write ratio comes from human behavior: a developer writes a paste once and shares the link with a team, a forum, or social media — dozens to thousands of viewers per paste. Power-law distribution amplifies this: top 1% of pastes (Stack Overflow answers, viral tweets) get 80% of total views.

quiz.question: Why store small pastes inline in DynamoDB instead of always using S3?

quiz.explanation: DynamoDB TTL is the primary mechanism — set ttl_epoch as a TTL attribute and AWS deletes the item within 48 h of the timestamp at no extra cost. The 48 h window is too loose for some users, so we also do a read-time check: if expires_at < now(), return 410 Gone immediately and delete the row (lazy delete on read).

quiz.explanation: PostgreSQL FTS works fine up to ~10 M rows but starts to degrade at 100 M+ — index rebuilds are slow, ranking quality is poor, and sharding requires Citus or manual partitioning. OpenSearch is purpose-built for inverted-index search: it scales horizontally (100+ nodes), supports analyzers per language (e.g., CJK tokenizer for Chinese code comments), and offers advanced ranking (BM25, function_score for time-decay).
